_comment: EPISODE 3c. Same takes, same grammars, same brand layer. Two edit rules now, both measured on the file in hand rather than assumed. (1) SHOT-ALIGNED re-cut, from ep3b: every boundary is one of the take's own picture cuts, so dropped dead air disappears on a shot change instead of jumping mid-shot. (2) A MINIMUM SHOT of 0.40s. ep3b passed the boundary check and still had a three-frame shot: a person change landed on a WIDE beat and the pace grammar's within-person reframe fired 0.10s later, so the wide beat was three frames and read as a stutter. Both of those cuts are the model's own, which is why the boundary check could not see it. The floor is derived from the tightest real EDIT in the reference set (Salary Transparent Street, 0.43s); SubwayTakes' 0.04s is one frame and is the detector firing twice on one transition, i.e. the same artefact being removed, so it is not used as a bound. ep3 and ep3b are kept on disk for comparison.
title: What's in the can
_output_comment: The output name carries all three seeds ON PURPOSE. build_looks.py's look filenames do not carry a seed and a seed-4816 build silently overwrote seed 4815's shipped deliverable once. This name cannot collide with episode 1 (4817-4819), episode 2 (4820-4822), any street-ld-*.mp4, or any 4815/4816/4823-4828 file.
_grade_comment: Not stored, same as episode 2. The episode is graded ONCE on the concatenated cut and the black lift is solved against that file by fit_grade.py at build time. A grade constant measured on one take outlives the take it was measured on (SKILL.md 19), and grading three takes separately is three curves across two joins, which is a visible step.
_ambience_comment: Not stored either, and this one has bitten twice (SKILL.md 13 and 21a): the speech-free window belongs to a FILE. build_episode.py finds it on the finished concatenation and asserts it is speech-free before cutting a bed or an end-card room tone from it.
